question_text: A legal-tech startup lets users upload one PDF contract at a time in a web app and ask questions about only that document during the session. The documents are not reused across users or sessions. The team wants answers grounded in the uploaded document with source attribution, minimal operational effort, and no vector database or ingestion pipeline to provision. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base with an Amazon OpenSearch Serverless collection, upload each document to its data source, and run an ingestion job per upload
Call the Amazon Bedrock RetrieveAndGenerate API with the uploaded document supplied as an external source, instead of a knowledge base
Generate embeddings for each document with Amazon Titan Embeddings and store them in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL pgvector table
Fine-tune a foundation model on each uploaded contract and invoke the resulting custom model

explanation: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases supports asking questions about, and summarizing, a single document without setting up a vector database; RetrieveAndGenerate accepts the document as an external source and returns a grounded answer with source attribution. A knowledge base on OpenSearch Serverless or a pgvector table both require provisioning and loading a vector store, which is unnecessary for one-off documents. Fine-tuning per document is slow, costly, and does not provide source attribution.
